name: Dino Campana
bio: Dino Campana (Marradi, 20 August 1885 – Castel Pulci, near Scandicci, 1 March 1932) was an Italian poet. He studied chemistry in Bologna and Florence, but a restless and troubled youth led him to wander through Europe and South America, and he was repeatedly confined to psychiatric hospitals.

His only book, Canti Orfici, appeared in 1914 at Marradi from the small press of Ravagli; it mingles visionary prose and verse, and it has come to be counted among the major works of Italian modernism. From 1918 until his death he lived in the asylum of Castel Pulci.
